title: Motion-o: Trajectory-Grounded Video Reasoning
claim: Fluent reasoning traces lack grounding; interleaving spatial, temporal and trajectory evidence with motion tags makes video reasoning explicit and verifiable.
layout: Stacked: video frames with trajectory arrows on top, question, answer, then reasoning box
description: The figure is headed by the title 'Motion-o: Video Frames + Spatial-Temporal-Trajectory Evidence Chain'. Below it, three real playground video frames (t=0.50s, 3.50s, 7.50s) show a girl in a pink box. Stacks of translucent blue frame planes sit between them. Dashed blue boxes mark the girl's position across frames, linked by black curved arrows and small magenta direction arrows. A question follows: 'What is the girl's trajectory across the playground?', then the ground-truth answer in plain text. The bottom half is a rounded light-green box labeled 'Motion-o'. It holds a <think> trace with inline monospace tags: obj, box coordinates, and timestamps in blue, and a pink <motion dir="E" speed="fast" scale="stable"/> tag. The caption 'Motion Chain of Thought (MCoT)' sits at the bottom. The eye goes first to the frames and arrows, then to the dense green text box.
caption: Although recent video models can produce fluent reasoning traces, their reasoning is typically ungrounded. Motion-o introduces a Spatial--Temporal--Trajectory (STT) evidence chain that explicitly embeds model reasoning with a trajectory-faithful trace.
abstract: Recent video reasoning models increasingly produce spatio-temporal evidence chains that localize objects at specific timestamps. While these traces improve interpretability by grounding \emph{where} and \emph{when} evidence appears, they often leave the motion connecting observations, the \textit{how}, implicit. This makes dynamic and trajectory-dependent claims difficult to supervise, verify, or penalize when unsupported by the video. We formalize this missing component as Spatial-Temporal-Trajectory (STT) reasoning and introduce \textbf{Motion-o}, a motion-centric extension to vision-language models (VLMs) that makes trajectories explicit and verifiable. Motion-o augments evidence chains with Motion Chain of Thought (MCoT), a structured pathway that represents object motion through a discrete \texttt{<motion/>} tag summarizing direction, speed, and scale change. To supervise MCoT, we densify sparse spatio-temporal annotations into object tracks and derive motion descriptors from centroid displacement and box-area change. We then train with complementary rewards for trajectory consistency and visual grounding, including a perturbation-based signal that penalizes motion descriptions that remain unchanged when temporal evidence is removed. Across multiple video understanding benchmarks, Motion-o consistently improves trajectory-faithful reasoning without architectural modifications. These results suggest that an explicit motion interface can complement existing VLM pipelines by converting implicit dynamics into verifiable evidence. Code is available at~\href{https://github.com/ostadabbas/Motion-o}{\faGithub\ \texttt{ostadabbas/Motion-o}}.
